title: SRE Weekly: Guardian Brief - 2028-09-12
content:
TL;DR: This week’s on-call rotation saw one medium-likelihood incident (INC-4782) affecting batched inference latency for the hosted API during a regional networking maintenance window. Impact: increased tail latency for ~3.2% of requests in us-west1 for 27 minutes. No customer data exposure. We consumed ~6% of the monthly error budget for the request-success SLO.

Key outcomes:
- Incident INC-4782 mitigated by reverting an aggressive autoscale policy change and rolling a conservative kernel selector patch (runtime v2.7.1 -> v2.7.1-rc3).
- Immediate runbook gaps identified around cross-zone routing: added a step to check edge-proxy connection pools before changing autoscale parameters.
- Owner assignments for follow-ups and a short action plan for next week.

1) Incident summary (INC-4782)
- Detection: 2028-09-10 08:14 UTC by synthetic latency alert (p95 > 350ms) and customer-reported slow requests in slack #prod-api.
- Affected surface: Hosted text-generation endpoints (api-route: /v1/generate) in us-west1.
- Impact window: 2028-09-10 08:12 UTC -> 08:39 UTC (27 minutes).
- User impact: ~3.2% of routed requests experienced p99 latency spikes (1.2–2.6s). Some streaming sessions timed out client-side.
- Root cause (prelim): Combination of a recent autoscale policy tweak (aggressive scale-down threshold) + transient packet loss between us-west1 worker pools and the region’s edge proxies during a colo partner maintenance. The scale-down thinned worker pools so batching latency increased; edge proxy retries amplified the effective request queueing.

Timeline (high-level):
- 08:12 UTC: synthetic alerts start rising; first customer ping at 08:14
- 08:16 UTC: on-call (Mateo Ruiz) triage — observed elevated queue depth and KV cache miss rates
- 08:20 UTC: rollback of autoscale change started (policy reverted to previous threshold)
- 08:26 UTC: kernel selector patch rolled (v2.7.1-rc3) to favor latency-optimized kernels for short-sequence workloads
- 08:35 UTC: p95 latency back within SLOs; 3 more minutes for queues to drain
- 08:39 UTC: incident declared mitigated; post-incident monitoring kept for 2h

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Reverted aggressive autoscale rule (owner: Priya Kapoor)
- Adjusted edge-proxy retry backoff temporarily (owner: Jonah Lee)
- Rolled runtime patch to select lower-latency kernels under high queue depth (owner: Mateo Ruiz)

Follow-up actions (owners & deadlines):
- Create a short runbook addendum for autoscale rollback steps and decision tree (owner: Priya Kapoor, due: 2028-09-18)
- Add a preflight check for edge-proxy connectivity before applying global autoscale changes (owner: Jonah Lee, due: 2028-09-19)
- Instrument per-zone batching metrics in the dashboard (owner: Sabrina Cole, due: 2028-09-21)
- Draft customer-facing incident note and review with comms (owner: Ava Martin, due: 2028-09-14)

2) SLO snapshot this week
- Request success SLO (hosted API, global): target 99.95% monthly; rolling window (30d) currently 99.89% -> error budget remaining ~20% for the month.
- Latency SLO (p95 global): target 350ms; rolling p95 this week: 342ms, spike on 2028-09-10 to 420ms during incident.
- Embedding throughput SLO: within target; observed small backlog during batch jobs on 2028-09-11 but recovered.

Notes/interpretation: small, contained consumption of error budget. The platform remains healthy but we should avoid risky autoscale pushes mid-week when colo partners may have maintenance windows. We should also add a policy to quiesce non-critical infra changes during partner-maintenance alerts.

3) On-call handoff highlights (next shift: 2028-09-12 16:00 UTC)
- Active follow-ups: runbook addendum (Priya), edge-proxy preflight check (Jonah), per-zone metrics (Sabrina).
- Ongoing experiments: measurement of KV cache hot-partitioning flagged by Mateo — potential config tweak to shard hashes (non-urgent).
- Open alerts to watch: synthetic latency monitors for /v1/generate in us-west1/us-east1; queue-depth > 2500 in any worker pool; kernel-fallback error rate > 0.5%.
- Pager escalation policy reminder: if p95 > 600ms for >10m or user-impacting errors > 1% for >5m, escalate to SRE lead (Ava) + runtime team.

Handoff checklist for incoming on-call:
- Read the incident slack thread pinned in #prod-api (link in linked_artifacts)
- Confirm synthetic monitors are green for all regions
- Check autoscale policy commit history for the last 72h (github: runbooks repo)
- Ensure on-call laptop has access to kernel-rollback playbooks and region-specific runbooks

4) Runbook and tooling notes
- Gap found: runbook lacked a quick checklist for diagnosing multi-hop proxy-induced latency. Added item: "curl edge-proxy /health and edge-proxy->worker RTT check".
- Proposal: add a lightweight preflight script that runs before autoscale policy changes (script should check edge-proxy connectivity, current queue depth, recent packet-loss events). Prototype PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks#312 (see linked_artifacts).

5) Operational risks & suggestions
- Risk: making autoscale and kernel-selector changes in the middle of third-party maintenance can multiply latency effects. Mitigation: coordinate change windows with colo partner maintenance—automate a blocker in our CI if partner-maintenance flag is set for the region.
- Risk: thin worker pools under aggressive scale-down thresholds increase p99 latency for streaming workloads. Mitigation: enforce a minimum healthy worker pool size for streaming routes.

6) Misc notes / scratchpad (informal)
- Quick wins: reduce default edge-proxy retry factor from 3 -> 2 for non-idempotent routes to reduce amplified queueing during transient issues.
- Unresolved: KV cache hot-key sharding pattern — Mat to prototype sharding config next sprint.
- FYI: hosted-console traces show an uptick in user retries correlating with the 08:12 window; CS has a handful of tickets; I'll draft the customer summary tomorrow.

7) Meeting follow-ups for next week
- Ops sync Tue 2028-09-19: present runbook addendum and proposed preflight script (owner: Priya)
- Reliability retro Fri 2028-09-22: include incident RCA draft + partner coordination checklist (owner: Ava)

Appendix: useful links and artifacts (repeat)
- Incident ticket: linear/RW/INC-4782 (link above)
- Runbook PR: github runbooks PR#312
- SLO dashboard: confluence KB link (dashboard and historical windows)

Notes to self: keep the incident note concise when sending to comms; avoid technical overload for customers. Emphasize mitigation, no data exposure, timeline, and next steps.

— End of brief —

Prepared by: Ava Martin (SRE Lead)
